Get the probability of each edge belonging to each component

Source: R/bison_mixture.R
get_edge_component_probabilities.Rd

For a mixture with a given number of components, returns the posterior probability that each edge belongs to each component (type of relationship). The probabilities include the uncertainty in both the edge weights and the mixture. Use it to classify edges, for example as weak or strong bonds.

Usage

get_edge_component_probabilities(object, num_components)

Arguments

object

A bison_mixture object from bison_mixture().

num_components

The number of components in the mixture to use, between 1 and the num_components used in bison_mixture(). This is often the most probable number, from get_network_component_probabilities().

Value

A data frame with one row per dyad, columns node_1 and node_2, and one column per component (P(component 1), ...). Each row sums to 1. Components are in increasing order of their mean.

See also

bison_mixture(), get_component_means()

Examples

sim_data <- simulate_bison_model_mixture(
  "count", num_components = 2, component_weights = c(0.5, 0.5)
)
fit_edge <- bison_model(
  (event | effort) ~ dyad(node_1_id, node_2_id),
  data = sim_data$df_sim,
  model_type = "count_conjugate",
  priors = get_default_priors("count_conjugate")
)
fit_mixture <- bison_mixture(fit_edge, num_components = 3, verbose = FALSE)
head(get_edge_component_probabilities(fit_mixture, 2))
#>   node_1 node_2 P(component 1) P(component 2)
#> 1      1      2              0              1
#> 2      1      3              1              0
#> 3      1      4              0              1
#> 4      1      5              1              0
#> 5      1      6              1              0
#> 6      1      7              0              1
